messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT  prod-inference elevated 5xx across regions; spike concentrated after automated failover. paging @Harper (oncall). :rotating_light:
Harper (Oncall): taking. pulling dashboards and routing state now. what's the scope?
Lena (SRE): seeing sudden 502/504s and long connect times beginning ~11:39Z. majority of errors spike in ap-northeast-1 and eu-west-1; traces show many connections still terminating to the original us-east-1 endpoints. Grafana: http://grafana/redwood/d/inf-failover
route-bot: ROUTE: automated failover triggered at 11:38Z from us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 due to detected capacity issue. subsequent BGP updates show AS path preference moved some traffic to ap-northeast-1 unexpectedly.
Diego (NetEng): yep, provider's community mapping for our failover communities was different than expected. some upstreams interpreted prefer-eu as prefer-ap and steered ~12% of traffic to ap-northeast, creating split traffic and overloading that warm standby.
Pri (Support): customers reporting timeouts and increased retries. currently 8 orgs >1% errors; 2 enterprise customers reporting degraded latency. AMs notified. sending interim message.
Harper (Oncall): classify P1 (multi-region degraded). mitigation plan: 1) stop automated failover and revert to manual routing, 2) traffic-shift away from overloaded ap-northeast to eu-west where capacity exists, 3) detach stuck backends in us-east to finish drains. initiating manual control now.
Diego (NetEng): pausing automation. applying explicit community to prefer eu-west for our prefixes and removing the prefer-ap tag. command: ```bgpctl set-community --prefixes all-inference --community prefer-eu --remove prefer-ap```
route-bot: ACTION: set-community applied at 11:44Z; propagation expected ~45s.
Lena (SRE): kicking off traffic-shift to eu-west-1 standby at 11:45Z: ```infra route shift --service inference --to eu-west-1 --percent 90 --mode manual``` watch KV caches and long-lived sessions during drain.
Harper (Oncall): shift started. errors drop globally but ap-northeast still showing elevated 5xx and CPU spike on warm hosts. some clients still pinned to us-east due to DNS TTLs.
Diego (NetEng): noticing that edge caches (public resolvers) are honoring old A-sets for up to 120s despite our 30s TTL. doubling down on route preference won't fix cached clients. We should fast-fail those stuck sessions at LB to unblock capacity.
Lena (SRE): agreed. capturing goroutine stacks and heap profiles before terminating. sample logs from stuck host ap-northeast-02:
```
2026-07-12T11:42:13Z inference[proc]: WARN session: persistent-stream from client-abc pinned
2026-07-12T11:42:27Z inference[proc]: ERROR drain: eviction timeout after 30s
```
Harper (Oncall): proceed with LB-level detach for targeted hosts. Diego, coordinate with edge to drop keepalives, then we'll restart service processes.
Diego (NetEng): detaching backends for ap-northeast-02 and ap-northeast-03 now: ```lbctl detach --pool inference-apn --hosts ap-northeast-02,ap-northeast-03```
Pri (Support): updating customers: "We've paused automated failover and are manually shifting traffic to eu-west. Targeted restarts happening to restore capacity; you may see brief retries." :white_check_mark:
Lena (SRE): detaches succeeded; collecting stacks to /var/log/traces then restarting processes: ```ssh op@ap-northeast-02 'gstack $pid > /tmp/stack.out; sudo systemctl restart inference'```
Harper (Oncall): restarts succeeded; drains cleared. traffic now ~92% eu-west, 6% us-east (DNS caches), 2% ap-northeast residual. overall 5xxs back near baseline.
route-bot: ROUTE: provider confirmed mis-mapped community for prefer-eu at 11:50Z; upstream rollback applied.
Diego (NetEng): provider admitted the mapping mismatch and rolled a fix; they've committed to a clarification on community semantics for our account. removing temporary community pins at 11:52Z.
Lena (SRE): verifying system health. p95 and p99 latency within SLOs, KV caches consistent. no data loss.
Pri (Support): customer impact window estimate: 11:38Z-11:52Z. created follow-up tickets CUST-11021 and CUST-11022; AMs updated.
Arjun (EM): good incident handling. assign postmortem owners: timeline (Lena), root cause and provider liaison (Diego), runbook automation changes (Harper), customer comms (Pri). Also actions: make failover automation require provider-community-claim verification, add LB auto-evict step after Xs of pinned sessions, and reduce critical DNS TTLs for inference endpoints during failover windows.
Harper (Oncall): handing off to Diego for monitoring and provider follow-up. handoff at 11:55Z. @Diego you're primary until 03:00Z.
Diego (NetEng): taking handoff. opening ticket to test provider community semantics in staging and to add a preflight check in our failover controller.
Lena (SRE): I'll draft the postmortem by EOD with logs, stacks, commands, and suggested automation for forced-evict after drain timeout.
Pri (Support): prepping customer timeline email for tomorrow with details and apologetic note.
route-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: services stable (11:56Z). incident resolved pending postmortem. :tada:
Harper (Oncall): thanks all. marking incident closed in channel. good coordination and fast mitigations.
Diego (NetEng): adding follow-up ticket for provider SLA and staging community tests.
Arjun (EM): scheduling 45min blameless review next week. please bring runbook edits and proposed automation"
